title: Setting your hourly rate and minimum charge for Deck and fence maintenance
audience: Owners of small Australian deck and fence maintenance businesses who need a base rate, an inspection minimum and a seasonal review before they quote.
learningOutcomes: Separate billable hours from non-billable hours, measured by season
Calculate a base hourly rate from the owner's own costs and income target, then check it against the evidence that exists
Set a minimum charge for an inspection visit, and explain it to a client before the visit

instruction.heading: What moves a deck and fence rate
instruction.body: A deck and fence rate depends on the materials handled, access, the condition of the structure and whether a permit or licence applies. The research did not find a deck- or fence-specific hourly rate. The Queensland and Victorian hourly figures found are for general handyman work, so do not use them as deck rates without checking your own costs. The Victorian vendor listing gives job-level estimates for deck work, which are a check on the total, not a rate.

instruction.heading: Count only the hours that can be billed
instruction.body: Site visits, measuring, quoting, set-up for sanding and cleaning, travel between sites, admin and equipment upkeep are not billable. Jobber says billable time typically makes up 60 to 80 per cent of working hours, which is a general range rather than an Australian figure. Seasonal work makes the billable count uneven, so measure billable hours by season before you choose a figure.

instruction.heading: Build the base rate from costs and income
instruction.body: Add running costs, including insurance, licence fees, the vehicle and trailer, tools and their upkeep, phone, software, marketing and accounting, and the income you need, including on-costs. Divide the total by billable hours. Confirm the tax and leave treatment with a registered tax agent. The ATO's small business benchmarks show labour and other costs as shares of turnover for many industries. Use them to check whether your labour share is out of line, and read your own industry's range rather than assuming one.

instruction.heading: Set a minimum charge for an inspection visit
instruction.body: An inspection visit has a cost that does not shrink with the size of the job. The Victorian vendor listing gives a structural inspection and quote at $250 to $600 (The Quote Yard, 2 May 2026). Set your inspection minimum so that travel, the inspection, the photo record and the report time are covered, and state it before the visit. Decide whether the inspection fee is credited against later work, and write that rule down.

instruction.heading: Review the rate each season
instruction.body: Review the rate about every three months (Business Victoria, undated), and at least once a year. Give repeat clients notice of a rise, and honour quotes already approved at the old rate. Keep a dated record of each change.

procedure: Log one season of paid hours and billable hours to find the billable share.
List the annual running costs, including insurance, licence fees, vehicle, tools, phone, software and marketing.
Add the income you need, including on-costs for leave and superannuation as confirmed by a registered tax agent.
Divide the total by the billable hours to find the base rate.
Set an inspection minimum that covers travel, inspection and report time, and state it in writing.
Review the rate each quarter and each season, and record any change and the reason for it.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only. An owner has 1,300 billable hours a year after deducting travel, quoting, admin and leave (illustrative). Annual running costs are $35,000 and the income target before tax is $75,000 (both illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the base rate? Is it safe to use a Queensland handyman rate of $65 to $120 as the deck rate instead?
workedExamples.reasoning: The total to recover is $110,000. Divided by 1,300 billable hours, the base rate is $84.62 an hour (illustrative). The Queensland vendor range of $65 to $120 is for handyman work, not deck restoration, so it is not a deck benchmark. Using it as the deck rate would ignore the owner's own costs, which is the error this lesson warns against. The owner's own base rate is the starting point. The full-job vendor estimate for a 20 square metre deck board renewal, $1,800 to $5,500 (Victoria, 2 May 2026), is a check on the total job price, and it is not a rate.

equipmentAndPpe: Log of paid and billable hours for one season
Price sheet with the base rate, the inspection minimum and the review date

commonErrors.error: Using a handyman or trade rate from a listing as the deck rate, without checking the costs.
commonErrors.prevention: Build the base rate from the owner's own costs and billable hours, then compare it with the evidence for the work.

commonErrors.error: Pricing as though every paid hour could be billed, including the slow winter months.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure billable hours by season, and subtract the non-billable time before dividing.

commonErrors.error: Offering a free inspection with no stated terms, so the visit cost is never covered.
commonErrors.prevention: Set and state an inspection minimum, and write down whether it is credited against later work.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited, and that a single advertised price should include any additional charges. The material read for this variant does not address minimum or inspection charges. Check those points with current ACCC guidance or a legal adviser before publishing a price sheet.
Confirm the tax treatment of leave and superannuation for your own situation with a registered tax agent before the rate is published.

A rate does not authorise work outside your licence. In Queensland, decks and verandahs need home-warranty cover when the project cost is more than $3,300 including GST, and building work above $3,300 needs a licence. In New South Wales, minor maintenance above $5,000 in labour and materials including GST needs a licence, and the research did not check whether deck or fence work falls within that definition. Check each state where you work.

qualityStandard: Billable hours are calculated from a logged season, not assumed.
The base rate is built from the owner's costs and income target, and is compared with the evidence available.
An inspection minimum is set and stated before any inspection visit.
documentationEvidence: Annual costs and income worksheet, with the source and date of each cost
Billable hours calculation by season, showing the non-billable deductions
Price sheet showing the base rate, the inspection minimum and the review date
summary: Price from billable hours, not from paid hours, and measure them by season.
Build the rate from costs and a stated income target, then check it against the evidence available.
Set and state an inspection minimum before any visit.

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner can bill only some of the paid hours. How should the rate be built?
options: From all paid hours, so the rate looks lower
From billable hours, so the costs and income are covered by the work that can be billed
From a handyman rate listed by a vendor, without any check on costs
From the rate the owner would like the market to pay

knowledgeChecks.question: Why set a minimum charge for an inspection visit?
options: Because an inspection needs no travel or report time
Because travel, inspection and report time does not shrink with the size of the job
Because clients expect every visit to cost the same amount
Because a minimum charge replaces a written quote

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a Queensland handyman hourly range a poor basis for a deck rate?
options: Because handyman ranges are always lower than deck rates
Because it is a range for general handyman work, not for deck restoration, and it ignores the owner's own costs
Because the ACCC prohibits using any vendor figure
Because deck work is never priced by the hour

sourceReferences: Jobber Academy, 'What are billable hours', https://getjobber.com/academy/what-are-billable-hours/, published 5 November 2024, last modified 20 July 2026. Billable time typically 60 to 80 per cent of working hours; general range, not Australian.

business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. On-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

ATO, 'Types of small business benchmarks', https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/small-business-benchmarks/types-of-benchmarks, last updated 17 March 2025. Labour and other costs as shares of turnover; no trade-specific figure taken.

The Quote Yard, Timber deck repair and restoration Victoria, https://www.thequoteyard.com.au/services/timber-deck-repair-and-restoration-carpentry-vic, published 2 May 2026. Vendor estimates for structural inspection and deck board renewal; used as checks on the total.
The Quote Yard, Handyman services QLD, https://www.thequoteyard.com.au/services/handyman-services-qld, published 10 May 2026. Vendor hourly range for handyman work; not a deck rate.

Business Victoria, 'Develop a pricing strategy', https://business.vic.gov.au/business-information/finance/pricing-for-profit/develop-a-pricing-strategy, no date shown. Review prices about every three months.
Queensland Building and Construction Commission, 'Home warranty cover', https://www.qbcc.qld.gov.au/node/2886, last reviewed 1 August 2024. Decks and verandahs above $3,300 including GST.

NSW Government, 'Minor maintenance and cleaning work', https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/licences-and-credentials/building-and-trade-licences-and-registrations/minor-maintenance-and-cleaning-work, last updated 23 June 2026. Licence above $5,000 in labour and materials including GST.
